problem: The sentence 'the delay ends when heat release becomes visible on the pressure trace' is imprecise: heat release is not directly visible on a pressure trace, and a student may confuse the pressure trace with a heat-release curve.
fix: The delay ends at the first measurable departure of the cylinder pressure from the motoring curve; heat release is calculated from that pressure trace.

problem: 'The third is the main phase and controls torque' is imprecise. Torque is set mainly by the fuel quantity; the main phase releases most of the heat and does most of the work.
fix: The third stage is the main phase: it releases most of the heat and does most of the work, while torque is set mainly by the fuel quantity.

problem: The bullet says the same delay in milliseconds covers more crank degrees at higher speed, but it does not say that the delay in milliseconds itself usually falls as speed rises, so a student may misread it as a simple scaling rule.
fix: At higher speed the delay in milliseconds usually falls; express the measured delay in crank degrees at that speed and do not scale a low-speed value.

problem: The answer gives ignition delay only as a time, but the chapter itself uses both milliseconds and crank degrees; the definition is incomplete for exam use.
fix: Time (or crank angle) from the start of injection to the first measurable pressure rise due to combustion; θd = 6 N td.
